primary_checks.assumptions: n>=2; prime target p; q denotes a place; source local density denominator q^{k(n^2-1)}.
logic: For q not dividing m, left multiplication by diag(u,1,...,1), with u a unit modulo q^k, bijects determinant fibers with values differing by the unit u. The determinant map is smooth at an invertible matrix, so each solution modulo q lifts to q^{(k-1)(n^2-1)} solutions of a fixed unit determinant modulo q^k.

The normalized unit density is beta_q=q^{-(n^2-1)}#SL_n(F_q)=product_{j=2}^n(1-q^{-j}). Counting independent ordered columns gives #GL_n(F_q)=product_{i=0}^{n-1}(q^n-q^i), and dividing by q-1 counts each nonzero determinant fiber.

The displayed equalities on pp10-11 omit q^{-(n^2-1)} from #GL_n(F_q)/(q-1). For n=2,q=2 and any odd target p, the actual normalized density is 6/8=3/4, whereas the printed right side is 6. The correctly normalized Bateman-Horn Euler factor was already printed on p9.

At q=p with target determinant exactly p mod p^k, a mod-p matrix of rank <=n-2 cannot contribute for k>=2: every lift has at least two p-divisible Smith invariant factors, hence determinant divisible by p^2. Rank n-1 matrices are nonsingular points of det=0 and each contributes p^{(k-1)(n^2-1)} lifts with the specified determinant.

The number of rank n-1 matrices over F_p is [(p^n-1)/(p-1)] product_{i=0}^{n-2}(p^n-p^i): choose a one-dimensional kernel, then an injective map from the (n-1)-dimensional quotient into F_p^n. Dividing this count by p^{n^2-1} gives delta_p=beta_p(1+p^{-1}+...+p^{-(n-1)}).

Consequently, with the corrected normalization, S_p=S_det(1+p^{-1}+...+p^{-(n-1)}). This proves the required stability with O(p^{-1}), stronger than the printed O(p^{-1/2}), without using an uninspected Lang-Weil reference.

There is no fixed-prime local obstruction for the determinant family: diag(m,1,...,1) realizes every integer m. The convergent product S_det=product_{j=2}^n zeta(j)^{-1} is positive, since the local deviations are O(q^{-2}).
primary_checks.correction: Insert q^{-(n^2-1)} in both displayed normalized unit-density identities on pp10-11. The exact rank-count calculation supplies a direct check of the bad-place stability used in the prime sum.
primary_checks.limits: This is a local count, not a new proof of the homogeneous-dynamics equidistribution theorem or an unconditional certification of the global theorem. It concerns the integer matrix lattice with the usual coordinate volume.

logic: The lattice of alternating 2n by 2n matrices has D=binom(2n,2)=2n^2-n independent coordinates. A nonsingular fixed-Pfaffian fiber has dimension D-1, so its counting density must use q^{k(D-1)}.

Theorem 3.5 instead prints q^{k(n^2-1)}. For n=2, write the six independent entries as a,b,c,d,e,f with Pfaffian af-be+cd. Over F_q, the equation Pf=1 has exactly (q^3-1)q^2 solutions: choose nonzero (a,b,c), then solve the nonzero linear equation in (f,-e,d).
Every Pf=1 point is smooth because a gradient vector could vanish only if all six entries vanished, impossible on that fiber. Hence the number modulo q^k is (q^3-1)q^2 q^{5(k-1)}.

For q=3 the correctly normalized density is 26/27. Dividing by the printed q^{3k} instead of q^{5k} gives (26/27)3^{2k}, which diverges. This is an explicit local calculation for n=2 in the theorem's allowed range, with no appeal to unseen literature.
The correction is q^{k(2n^2-n-1)}, agreeing with the general q^{k dim(V_m)} normalization on p7 and with the m^{2n-2} exponent already printed in Theorem 3.5.
The source's diagonal-congruence map scales the Pfaffian by the unit b, not b^2: each monomial uses the first index exactly once. This validates the unit-fiber bijection at the algebraic level.
Block diagonal matrices diag(mJ,J,...,J), J=[[0,1],[-1,0]], realize every integer m as Pfaffian, so there is no fixed-prime obstruction in the integral alternating lattice.

logic: Let n=2r+1 be odd and ell an odd prime. The Jordan blocks have ranks 2r and 1. Write chi=(((-1)^r det(f0))/ell), which is plus or minus one because f0 is unimodular.

primary_checks.target: Exact direct rank-four 2-adic density, without assuming a mass formula
primary_checks.status: Analytical derivation plus actual exhaustive finite calculation
analytic_derivation: Enumerate Sym_4(F_2): the actual own-script count finds 448 invertible matrices, of which 28 are alternating and 420 nonalternating. The rank calculation is exact binary Gaussian elimination over all 2^10 independent-entry choices.

For a nonalternating invertible symmetric matrix modulo 2, its inverse is also nonalternating: otherwise x^T A^-1 x=0 for all x, and setting x=Ay would force y^T Ay=0 for all y. Therefore some diagonal cofactor is odd. The determinant has a unit partial derivative in a diagonal coordinate, so each fixed odd determinant fiber has 2^9 lifts at each step. Its normalized Type-I contribution is 420/2^9=105/128, independent of the odd target.

Every invertible alternating matrix modulo 2 is congruent to H=diag(J,J), J=[[0,1],[1,0]]. A lift of the congruence matrix to GL_4(Z/8Z) has odd determinant, whose square is 1 modulo 8, so congruence preserves the target determinant residue modulo 8. All 28 alternating residue classes therefore have the same lift counts.
Write S=H+2B. Since det(H)=1 and H^-1=H, expanding det(I+2HB) modulo 8 gives 1+2 tr(HB)+4 e_2(HB). For symmetric B this simplifies to det(S)=1+4(B11 B22+B33 B44) modulo 8.

The formula depends only on B modulo 2. Each diagonal pair has three choices with product zero and one with product one; equal products occur in 3*3+1*1=10 of 16 diagonal choices, and unequal products in 6. The six independent off-diagonal bits are free, giving 640 binary B with determinant 1 modulo 8 and 384 with determinant 5. The script checks the formula against exact signed-permutation determinants for all 1024 B.

Each binary B has 2^10 extensions modulo 4. Thus the Type-II counts modulo 8 are 28*2^10*640 and 28*2^10*384 for target residues 1 and 5; residues 3 and 7 receive no Type-II contribution. Dividing by 8^9 gives 35/256 and 21/256.

These mod-8 densities stabilize. For any invertible alternating reduction choose an off-diagonal cofactor that is odd; the symmetric-coordinate derivative of det is twice that cofactor. For k>=3, perturb that coordinate by 2^{k-1}. This preserves det modulo 2^k and flips its next bit modulo 2^{k+1}; the quadratic remainder is divisible by 2^{2k-2}, hence by 2^{k+1}. The perturbation pairs solutions modulo 2^k into the two possible next determinant bits.

For Type II all determinant partial derivatives are even, so all 2^10 lifts of a matrix modulo 2^k have the same determinant modulo 2^{k+1}. Exactly half of the solutions at level k lift to the specified next bit; hence N_{k+1}=2^9 N_k and the normalized density is constant from k=3 onward.
Adding Type I yields total fixed-unit densities delta_2(a): 245/256 for a=1, 105/128 for a=3, 231/256 for a=5, and 105/128 for a=7 modulo 8.

Their mean is 7/8. Independently, the directly counted Bateman-Horn factor at 2 is (448/1024)/(1-1/2)=7/8. This verifies the local normalization and the aggregate residue-class matching in this lowest even-rank case.

notation.odd_zeta_product: S_n=product over odd j, 3<=j<=n, of zeta(j)^-1
notation.L_convention: L_odd(r,chi_ell)=sum over odd m with (m,ell)=1 of (((-1)^r ell)/m)m^{-r}; the Euler factor at 2 is omitted.

logic: The p20 convention sets the local Legendre symbol to zero when the place divides 2D, and p30 explicitly expands only odd m. Thus the final cancellation is checked using L_odd. Replacing this by a primitive L-function with a nontrivial factor at 2 without compensating the branch constants would change the calculation; no such replacement is made.

For each fixed odd nonsquare m, the Jacobi symbol as a function of the prime ell is a nonprincipal character modulo an odd divisor of m. Restricting ell to one reduced residue class modulo 8 does not trivialize it, by the Chinese remainder theorem. The prime number theorem in fixed arithmetic progressions therefore gives a zero weighted mean for this term.
For m=t^2 with t odd, the character is one except at primes dividing t, whose contribution for fixed t is finite. The square coefficients sum to sum_{t odd}t^{-n}=(1-2^{-n})zeta(n).

The exchange of summation and limiting mean can be justified with a fixed cutoff M: for r>=2 the absolute tail is bounded uniformly in ell by sum_{m>M}m^{-r}, which tends to zero. For the finite head use only fixed-modulus prime number theorems, then let M tend to infinity. This proves the leading o(1) mean without claiming the source's uniform log^{-101} estimates were externally verified.
Consequently, for each a0 modulo 8 with gcd(a0,8)=1, sum_{ell<=T^n,ell=a0 mod8} L_odd(r,chi_ell)ell^{(n-1)/2} ~ [(1-2^{-n})zeta(n)/4] A(T).

The three branch multipliers from the corrected equations (16)-(18) are C0=1 if ell is not congruent to epsilon modulo4; Cplus=1+2^{1-n}/(1-x) if ell=epsilon modulo4 and ell=plus/minus1 modulo8; Cminus=1+2^{1-n}/(1+x) for the remaining eligible class. There are respectively two, one and one reduced residue classes, for either parity of r.
The class-weighted multiplier is (1-x^2)[1/2+(1/4)(1+2x^2/(1-x))+(1/4)(1+2x^2/(1+x))]=1. Indeed the bracket equals 1+x^2/(1-x^2)=1/(1-x^2).

Multiplying Corollary 7.3's factor 2 by Proposition 7.4's one-half leaves no extra one-half. With that correction, the odd-zeta product S_n remains and the averaged cone count is psi(u,v) mu_F(Omega) S_n A(T)(1+o(1)), agreeing with the coarea prime integral.

auxiliary_bounded_checks.target: Local density stability and local obstructions for determinant prime levels
auxiliary_bounded_checks.status: Corrected local stability checked analytically, including an exact formula
auxiliary_bounded_checks.assumptions: n>=2; prime target p; q denotes a place; source local density denominator q^{k(n^2-1)}.
logic: For q not dividing m, left multiplication by diag(u,1,...,1), with u a unit modulo q^k, bijects determinant fibers with values differing by the unit u. The determinant map is smooth at an invertible matrix, so each solution modulo q lifts to q^{(k-1)(n^2-1)} solutions of a fixed unit determinant modulo q^k.

The normalized unit density is beta_q=q^{-(n^2-1)}#SL_n(F_q)=product_{j=2}^n(1-q^{-j}). Counting independent ordered columns gives #GL_n(F_q)=product_{i=0}^{n-1}(q^n-q^i), and dividing by q-1 counts each nonzero determinant fiber.

The displayed equalities on pp10-11 omit q^{-(n^2-1)} from #GL_n(F_q)/(q-1). For n=2,q=2 and any odd target p, the actual normalized density is 6/8=3/4, whereas the printed right side is 6. The correctly normalized Bateman-Horn Euler factor was already printed on p9.

At q=p with target determinant exactly p mod p^k, a mod-p matrix of rank <=n-2 cannot contribute for k>=2: every lift has at least two p-divisible Smith invariant factors, hence determinant divisible by p^2. Rank n-1 matrices are nonsingular points of det=0 and each contributes p^{(k-1)(n^2-1)} lifts with the specified determinant.

The number of rank n-1 matrices over F_p is [(p^n-1)/(p-1)] product_{i=0}^{n-2}(p^n-p^i): choose a one-dimensional kernel, then an injective map from the (n-1)-dimensional quotient into F_p^n. Dividing this count by p^{n^2-1} gives delta_p=beta_p(1+p^{-1}+...+p^{-(n-1)}).

Consequently, with the corrected normalization, S_p=S_det(1+p^{-1}+...+p^{-(n-1)}). This proves the required stability with O(p^{-1}), stronger than the printed O(p^{-1/2}), without using an uninspected Lang-Weil reference.

There is no fixed-prime local obstruction for the determinant family: diag(m,1,...,1) realizes every integer m. The convergent product S_det=product_{j=2}^n zeta(j)^{-1} is positive, since the local deviations are O(q^{-2}).
auxiliary_bounded_checks.correction: Insert q^{-(n^2-1)} in both displayed normalized unit-density identities on pp10-11. The exact rank-count calculation supplies a direct check of the bad-place stability used in the prime sum.

logic: The lattice of alternating 2n by 2n matrices has D=binom(2n,2)=2n^2-n independent coordinates. A nonsingular fixed-Pfaffian fiber has dimension D-1, so its counting density must use q^{k(D-1)}.

Theorem 3.5 instead prints q^{k(n^2-1)}. For n=2, write the six independent entries as a,b,c,d,e,f with Pfaffian af-be+cd. Over F_q, the equation Pf=1 has exactly (q^3-1)q^2 solutions: choose nonzero (a,b,c), then solve the nonzero linear equation in (f,-e,d).
Every Pf=1 point is smooth because a gradient vector could vanish only if all six entries vanished, impossible on that fiber. Hence the number modulo q^k is (q^3-1)q^2 q^{5(k-1)}.

For q=3 the correctly normalized density is 26/27. Dividing by the printed q^{3k} instead of q^{5k} gives (26/27)3^{2k}, which diverges. This is an explicit local calculation for n=2 in the theorem's allowed range, with no appeal to unseen literature.
The correction is q^{k(2n^2-n-1)}, agreeing with the general q^{k dim(V_m)} normalization on p7 and with the m^{2n-2} exponent already printed in Theorem 3.5.
The source's diagonal-congruence map scales the Pfaffian by the unit b, not b^2: each monomial uses the first index exactly once. This validates the unit-fiber bijection at the algebraic level.
Block diagonal matrices diag(mJ,J,...,J), J=[[0,1],[-1,0]], realize every integer m as Pfaffian, so there is no fixed-prime obstruction in the integral alternating lattice.

logic: Let n=2r+1 be odd and ell an odd prime. The Jordan blocks have ranks 2r and 1. Write chi=(((-1)^r det(f0))/ell), which is plus or minus one because f0 is unimodular.
Substitution in the displayed equation (11) gives alpha_ell(S)^-1=(1/(2ell))(1-chi ell^-r)^-1 product_{i=1}^{r-1}(1-ell^-2i)^-1.

symmetric_auxiliary_checks.target: Exact direct rank-four 2-adic density, without assuming a mass formula
symmetric_auxiliary_checks.status: Analytical derivation plus actual exhaustive finite calculation
analytic_derivation: Enumerate Sym_4(F_2): the actual own-script count finds 448 invertible matrices, of which 28 are alternating and 420 nonalternating. The rank calculation is exact binary Gaussian elimination over all 2^10 independent-entry choices.

For a nonalternating invertible symmetric matrix modulo 2, its inverse is also nonalternating: otherwise x^T A^-1 x=0 for all x, and setting x=Ay would force y^T Ay=0 for all y. Therefore some diagonal cofactor is odd. The determinant has a unit partial derivative in a diagonal coordinate, so each fixed odd determinant fiber has 2^9 lifts at each step. Its normalized Type-I contribution is 420/2^9=105/128, independent of the odd target.

Every invertible alternating matrix modulo 2 is congruent to H=diag(J,J), J=[[0,1],[1,0]]. A lift of the congruence matrix to GL_4(Z/8Z) has odd determinant, whose square is 1 modulo 8, so congruence preserves the target determinant residue modulo 8. All 28 alternating residue classes therefore have the same lift counts.
Write S=H+2B. Since det(H)=1 and H^-1=H, expanding det(I+2HB) modulo 8 gives 1+2 tr(HB)+4 e_2(HB). For symmetric B this simplifies to det(S)=1+4(B11 B22+B33 B44) modulo 8.

The formula depends only on B modulo 2. Each diagonal pair has three choices with product zero and one with product one; equal products occur in 3*3+1*1=10 of 16 diagonal choices, and unequal products in 6. The six independent off-diagonal bits are free, giving 640 binary B with determinant 1 modulo 8 and 384 with determinant 5. The script checks the formula against exact signed-permutation determinants for all 1024 B.

Each binary B has 2^10 extensions modulo 4. Thus the Type-II counts modulo 8 are 28*2^10*640 and 28*2^10*384 for target residues 1 and 5; residues 3 and 7 receive no Type-II contribution. Dividing by 8^9 gives 35/256 and 21/256.

These mod-8 densities stabilize. For any invertible alternating reduction choose an off-diagonal cofactor that is odd; the symmetric-coordinate derivative of det is twice that cofactor. For k>=3, perturb that coordinate by 2^{k-1}. This preserves det modulo 2^k and flips its next bit modulo 2^{k+1}; the quadratic remainder is divisible by 2^{2k-2}, hence by 2^{k+1}. The perturbation pairs solutions modulo 2^k into the two possible next determinant bits.

For Type II all determinant partial derivatives are even, so all 2^10 lifts of a matrix modulo 2^k have the same determinant modulo 2^{k+1}. Exactly half of the solutions at level k lift to the specified next bit; hence N_{k+1}=2^9 N_k and the normalized density is constant from k=3 onward.
Adding Type I yields total fixed-unit densities delta_2(a): 245/256 for a=1, 105/128 for a=3, 231/256 for a=5, and 105/128 for a=7 modulo 8.

Their mean is 7/8. Independently, the directly counted Bateman-Horn factor at 2 is (448/1024)/(1-1/2)=7/8. This verifies the local normalization and the aggregate residue-class matching in this lowest even-rank case.

notation.odd_zeta_product: S_n=product over odd j, 3<=j<=n, of zeta(j)^-1
notation.L_convention: L_odd(r,chi_ell)=sum over odd m with (m,ell)=1 of (((-1)^r ell)/m)m^{-r}; the Euler factor at 2 is omitted.

logic: The p20 convention sets the local Legendre symbol to zero when the place divides 2D, and p30 explicitly expands only odd m. Thus the final cancellation is checked using L_odd. Replacing this by a primitive L-function with a nontrivial factor at 2 without compensating the branch constants would change the calculation; no such replacement is made.

For each fixed odd nonsquare m, the Jacobi symbol as a function of the prime ell is a nonprincipal character modulo an odd divisor of m. Restricting ell to one reduced residue class modulo 8 does not trivialize it, by the Chinese remainder theorem. The prime number theorem in fixed arithmetic progressions therefore gives a zero weighted mean for this term.
For m=t^2 with t odd, the character is one except at primes dividing t, whose contribution for fixed t is finite. The square coefficients sum to sum_{t odd}t^{-n}=(1-2^{-n})zeta(n).

The exchange of summation and limiting mean can be justified with a fixed cutoff M: for r>=2 the absolute tail is bounded uniformly in ell by sum_{m>M}m^{-r}, which tends to zero. For the finite head use only fixed-modulus prime number theorems, then let M tend to infinity. This proves the leading o(1) mean without claiming the source's uniform log^{-101} estimates were externally verified.
Consequently, for each a0 modulo 8 with gcd(a0,8)=1, sum_{ell<=T^n,ell=a0 mod8} L_odd(r,chi_ell)ell^{(n-1)/2} ~ [(1-2^{-n})zeta(n)/4] A(T).

The three branch multipliers from the corrected equations (16)-(18) are C0=1 if ell is not congruent to epsilon modulo4; Cplus=1+2^{1-n}/(1-x) if ell=epsilon modulo4 and ell=plus/minus1 modulo8; Cminus=1+2^{1-n}/(1+x) for the remaining eligible class. There are respectively two, one and one reduced residue classes, for either parity of r.
The class-weighted multiplier is (1-x^2)[1/2+(1/4)(1+2x^2/(1-x))+(1/4)(1+2x^2/(1+x))]=1. Indeed the bracket equals 1+x^2/(1-x^2)=1/(1-x^2).
